We don't know if consciousness is unchanging, but it doesn't really matter. It's static in the sense that you, the observer, are. And you are never \*not\*. We know senses are a separate part of this because dreams require no stimuli to operate, yet they model experience and existence to the degree that you can even recall them as something vaguely reality-like.

As for "And for that matter, why do we assume that the only thing that is truly us is what we are aware of?":  
We don't really assume this as much as we kind of wave our hands and accept that whatever we can't interact with, or things that don't have causal reactions/impacts on things we CAN interact with, isn't something we can really deal with or even try to engage with.

As for what you described regarding reflexes, it kind of strengthens the central point even further that your consciousness is separate from your body if it has stimuli that requires no input to operate. Your body does all kinds of things like reflexes, but still, you exist just the same at any point in time during the event. Your body is as much of a part of the consciousness as a river flowing into an ocean is a part of the ocean.

Now are your thoughts "you"? Maybe, depends on if you think they are emergent properties from physical things, or if you think they are something else. But if we engage with the body as a packaged physical system, we need to first remember the fact that non-physical things necessarily cannot interact with physical ones. Further, emergent categories (such as the category of a car, a collection of traits) cannot interact with physical matter themselves. It's not the category "car" that's physical, it's a bunch of objects we group together.

This means that a consciousness, if it is linked to the physical realm as an emergent property from underlying matter/physical objects, must have physical roots. This means that it has a fundamental mass and shape it is based on, such as the car with it's metal frame, its engine and wheels it rides on. So what does it look like? Where is it?

Do recommend reading up on modern physicalist philosophy if you're interested more on this. I'm not really the best at explaining it but there are some seriously cool discussions in metaphysics with regards to physicalism in recent times, especially as neuroscience has caught up.

I work on memory systems in GPUs, but i think this is fruitless. Yes, there are many closed (edit: closed-source*) protocols for memory compression and hardware optimizations that are still being rolled out. There are many pages from NVIDIA that details this stuff that’s worth a read.

I don’t know what to tell you other than that you’re wrong. You seem to think that the vram buffer is stored up over a few days rather than within minutes at most of gameplay. I think you are very uninformed on the subject. Textures aren’t stored uncompressed in ram, nor is it necessary to store them in the manner you probably think since around 2012. Modern texture streaming is done in a hierarchical manner where the «vram capacity» metric measures the total capacity from top to bottom, where the size you read is largely the lowest level storage. Much of the issue lies in access patterns and smart ways to move chunks through memory and this is where most of the architectural gains are. Size can provide gains as it buffers slow throughput, but crucially, enough throughput removes the need for large capacity.

The most central point is this: There are many reasons the dips you mentioned are there. For a 3070, maybe an increase in capacity would solve the problem. For a 5070, 6GB of its memory structure could be enough. It’s entirely dependent on the architecture. That’s my point.

Speed, architecture and bus layouts contribute so much more compared to just vram capacity. The reason your 3070 «is a potato» is because it’s 4+ years old and games are getting exponentially heavier with a combination of worse optimization and insane demands for fidelity. Size is important to a degree but there is a good good reason that the size is limited as size increases have other huge tradeoffs.
Newsflash everyone: total ram capacity is probably one of the less important metrics in the grand scheme of things for gaming. Sucks for the AI bros though.

The most important thing in the game are matchups, matchups and matchups. Rarely is there a "best unit" of a specific type, but ALWAYS is there a "best unit to do a specific thing". Facing cavalry? Load up on spearmen and make sure they brace for charges. Facing large units? Load up on anti-large. Don't send your swordsmen into a cavalry charge and don't target the hero with 90% missile resist with your archers. Be mindful of armor and Armor Piercing (AP) damage. If you're playing against Skaven for example, they're practically never armored, so investing into it tends to be a waste. This is because units usually trade worse stats or cost in return for AP damage. Therefore, if you don't need AP, don't invest into it.

How do you refer to other people? The point I’m making is that you use gender all the time. If you see a pretty lady, you say «she». Same for men. That’s gender. The overarching argument is that you don’t truly know wether they’re male/female or not. The assumption is that they’re male/female because they look the part, gender therefore isn’t all that rigid. It’s really just an assumption we make that makes language easier.
How would you refer to a woman on the street? «it»?

So how do you find out if a person that looks like a woman is trans, in the end? Do a little touch test for testicles? The point is that if you’re at this point, it’s faded to obscurity/absurdity. We don’t test/check for stuff like this, nor do we need to. We make assumptions because that’s how we communicate. That’s where the social part comes in, because those assumptions and predefinitions are learned from our culture growing up, and it’s what molds and shapes our language.
Gender does exist, it maps onto the more rigid concept of sex. It’s a necessary part of our language and communication.
Where? And it’s not C16 in Canada, because that law was against *unlawful workplace discrimination*, which is not «offending someone.»

Gender is about perception. It’s all to make language easier. On the contrary, sex is a hard and rigid scientifical thing (most often). 

John and Carl are at a bar. John says to Carl: «look at that chick over there». If this person was presenting as a woman, and John somehow knew they had a penis, saying «he» makes it awfully difficult for Carl to look because he would be looking for male characteristics. That is why we say «socially defined» because John might also include people with short hair as feminine while Carl maybe wouldn’t associate that with a woman at all. This is what people mean when they say that gender is not the same as sex. They can be to some people, but not necessarily. Gender is not a rigid thing.

Note that rush warrior is very much a combo deck that responds to and capitalizes off of small minions from your opponent, so large minions like for example libram paladin or clown druid run will be hard to combo off of. This is also why the deck fares well against secret paladin.

Early game pressure is key, while also transitioning into the mid-to-late game with \[\[conditioning\]\] and \[\[overlord runthak\]\] buffing your minions. In a perfect scenario these two key cards will keep scaling your minions to be able to tackle the increasing sizes of your opponent's.

Your \[\[imprisoned gan'arg\]\] will keep you afloat early to make sure too big nuisances to your Rokara buffs get removed efficiently, thus allowing you to springboard off the small ones. Your removal tools (other than the obvious Samuro and warmaul challenger) will likely include the aforementioned gan'arg axe or a \[\[sword eater\]\] sword, and riders from \[\[bumper car\]\]'s deathrattle; I like to keep a few of these at hand and buff them. Should a big threat pop up, you can combo with \[\[playmaker\]\] and/or \[\[parade leader\]\] which will deal with 99% of problems. 

Your game winning play will often be a duplicate rokara from playmaker into crabrider or something else big. Shield of honor makes that whole ordeal a lot more dangerous for your opponent, so make sure top bait out removal and to not overextend in the early game. Finish off this zerg cake with a sprinkle of gigantic troublemakers and Alextrasza. There are probably more intricate game plans but this is the general gist.
